A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DragFlow, with matching authors, methodology, benchmarks, and retained results. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original inversion experiments, evaluations on ReD Bench and DragBench-DR, component ablations, and qualitative editing results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds controlled comparisons, robustness analyses, runtime measurements, and backbone and identity-module experiments.

M1.justification: The standard DragFlow pipeline, losses, and optimization procedure remain unchanged. Appendix J.2 adds a procedural variant that first trains a subject-specific LoRA and then uses it instead of the pretrained identity adapter, constituting a limited method extension.

E1.justification: ReD Bench and DragBench-DR remain the evaluation datasets. V3 adds targeted scenarios involving absent or misleading prompts, inaccurate masks, intricate hair/clothing structures, and bending or sequential composite edits (Appendices D.4 and H.2-H.3), extending coverage within the existing editing task.

E2.justification: The nine external editing baselines remain unchanged. V3 adds an augmented point-based DiT comparator with background preservation and adapter enhancement (Table 4), unlike v1's unaugmented point-based ablation baseline. It also evaluates QWen-VL prompting and subject-specific LoRA alternatives in Tables 5 and 8.

E3.justification: The original metrics and editing schedule are retained. Added experiments introduce matched auxiliary-module controls, a feature-layer sweep, prompt manipulations, SD3.5 and LoRA configurations, and preparation-plus-edit time and peak-memory measurements on DragBench-DR using one H100 (Appendices C.5-C.6, D.4, I-J). These are new protocols, not demonstrated reruns of the original comparisons.

E4.justification: V1's cumulative component ablation and PCA visualizations are substantially extended by quantitative layer selection, controlled point-versus-region supervision, prompt ablations, mask-failure cases, complex-edit robustness examples, and backbone/identity-module analyses. These directly test several previously unexamined design choices and applicability boundaries.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's additional dataset averages and layer sweep do not introduce uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 retain their numerical results. V3 adds Tables 4-8 and qualitative findings: matched-module point/region MD1 scores are 37.02/31.59; SD3.5 and LoRA variants report MD1 of 35.21 and 30.98; runtime and memory are 158.7 seconds and 23.5 GB. These concern added conditions, not improvements to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical content in Equations 1-31 is retained, including supervision losses, affine transformations, region weighting, gradient masking, and metric definitions. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and superiority claims: DiT-based drag editing through region supervision, background constraints, adapter-enhanced inversion, and ReD Bench. The abstract's revised wording clarifies the existing rationale without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of prompt conflicts, compositional affine editing, cross-backbone applicability, and LoRA specialization, plus substantive limitations concerning mask precision and computational cost. The inversion-drift limitation remains. Separately, the introduction reverses its cited distortion comparison from SD outperforming GAN priors to GAN outperforming SD priors.

D1.justification: V3 replaces a future-release promise with reported code/dataset access, adds adapter resource links, and documents H100 hardware, qint8 quantization, and CPU offloading. Table 3 now identifies ReD Bench. Conversely, Appendix C.5 removes the exact KV-injection layer lists and caching instructions; this is lost documentation, not evidence that KV injection was removed.

R1.justification: Appendix A updates a limited citation set, adding works such as Target-aware Image Editing and LUVE while dropping AddSR and 3DIS-FLUX. The explicit FreeFlux implementation attribution in C.5 disappears. The main related-work taxonomy and positioning against RegionDrag remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 lightly revises the abstract and selected passages, adds acknowledgments and conference headers, and expands the appendix hierarchy with new analysis subsections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact; the scientific additions do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 adds five experimental tables, a three-panel layer-performance chart, failure/success comparisons, and a substantial challenging-scenario image grid. Existing figures are retained and sometimes relocated or renumbered. It also corrects PCA layer labels in Figures 7-8 and the dataset-example caption's row/column descriptions.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the central supervision rationale through the controlled comparison in Table 4 and quantitative layer sweep in Figure 9. Prompt tests, portability checks, and explicit failure and computational-cost analyses make the paper's effectiveness and practical boundaries considerably easier to assess. These gains outweigh the loss of exact KV-injection documentation, although uncertainty reporting and details for reproducing some new variants remain limited.
